note: Display numbers are assigned at assembly; artifact IDs are immutable.

artifacts.caption: Evidence-to-claim architecture of the HydroSheaf framework.
artifacts.technical_description: Layout declared as node and edge tables; no external graph layout engine. Box widths leave a visible surface gap between adjacent boxes in a row.
artifacts.interpretation: Candidate sets survive to the claim gate, which is the design property that permits an abstention rather than a forced resolution.

artifacts.caption: Location, analytical quality, facies and isotopic character of the three measured datasets.
artifacts.technical_description: Panel (a) is a projected map with administrative boundaries from the geoBoundaries database (CC BY 4.0), cached locally by fetch_boundaries.R so the figure renders offline. Scale bar, north arrow and a locator inset are included. Primary measured panels only. Local meteoric water lines are OLS fits drawn across each dataset's own isotopic range, never extrapolated.
artifacts.interpretation: The three datasets differ in analytical quality by an order of magnitude, and all three show evaporative isotopic enrichment.

artifacts.caption: Variable availability and the resulting evidence ceiling.
artifacts.technical_description: Categorical presence encoding rather than a continuous gradient, because almost every carried variable is fully populated and the informative contrast is absence.
artifacts.interpretation: The absent determinands, not the present ones, fix the field claim boundary.

artifacts.caption: Component recovery across 100 synthetic realisations with known truth.
artifacts.technical_description: Panels share a 1:1 reference line. Truth-zero reaction terms are drawn in grey so that leakage is visible against the active terms.
artifacts.interpretation: Transport and residence time are recoverable; point reaction extents are not.

artifacts.caption: Locked controlled-synthetic gate results and prospective decision utility.
artifacts.technical_description: Each metric is plotted against its own predeclared threshold on a common axis within the panel. Only contrasts with HydroSheaf as the left policy are shown.
artifacts.interpretation: All component gates met thresholds fixed before scoring; the paired intervals are within-run descriptive summaries.

artifacts.caption: Comparison against published lumped-parameter ages and a particle-tracking topology.
artifacts.technical_description: Uncalibrated and calibrated variants are shown as separate facets and never pooled. Topology modes are likewise faceted and colour-coded by whether the comparison is independent.
artifacts.interpretation: Independent agreement is screening-level; the calibrated panel measures emulation of the reference.

artifacts.caption: Field application: in-sample closure, retained alternatives and measurement value.
artifacts.technical_description: The closure axis extends below zero so that edges closing worse than the sample mean remain visible rather than being clipped.
artifacts.interpretation: The field output is a compatible-explanation set and a measurement-design constraint, not a validated mechanism.

artifacts.caption: Inventory of the three measured field datasets.
artifacts.technical_description: Charge-balance error recomputed independently from reported ions; Northern Ghana summarised as its 160-well primary panel.
artifacts.interpretation: Analytical quality, not sample count, is the binding constraint on the field application.

artifacts.caption: Implemented package capabilities and their claim scope.
artifacts.technical_description: Every row names a module present in the installed package.
artifacts.interpretation: Capability and claim scope are recorded together so that a software inventory is not read as an evidence inventory.

artifacts.caption: Locked gate results against thresholds fixed before scoring.
artifacts.technical_description: Observed values and thresholds are read from the locked run record; pass status is recomputed from the two rather than copied.
artifacts.interpretation: Thresholds are safety floors for a bounded claim, not evidence of optimality.

artifacts.caption: Quantities where recomputation disagreed with earlier internal reporting.
artifacts.technical_description: Generated from the discrepancy ledger written by the evidence derivation scripts.
artifacts.interpretation: Publishing the disagreement is a reproducibility statement; in every case the recomputed value stands.
